library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Weng_2015_PF05231023_obob_mouse_qsp"))$reference`
* Article: [PLoS One 2015;10(3):e0119104](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0119104) (open access)

PF-05231023 is a long-acting FGF21 analogue: two FGF21 molecules conjugated
(at A129C) to the CovX-2000 antibody scaffold. Proteases clip the FGF21
C-terminus quickly and the N-terminus slowly, so after dosing the circulating
drug is a mixture of fully intact molecules (high potency) and "N-only"
molecules (C-terminus clipped, still active at lower potency). Weng et al.
built two mechanistic PK/PD models on that idea, each in its own mouse model
and fitted separately, and both are packaged here:

| Model file | Mouse | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `Weng_2015_PF05231023_obob_mouse_qsp` | leptin-deficient ob/ob | glucose-AUC reduction in an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) |
| `Weng_2015_PF05231023_dio_mouse_qsp` | diet-induced obese (DIO) | body weight during and after three weekly doses |

```{r load-models}
obob <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Weng_2015_PF05231023_obob_mouse_qsp"))
dio <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Weng_2015_PF05231023_dio_mouse_qsp"))
obob$description
dio$description
```

Both models are deterministic: the paper fits mean responses by least
squares and reports no between-animal or residual variability, so every
simulation below is a single typical-animal solve.

# Population

All animals were male mice. PK was measured after single 3 or 10 mg/kg IV or
SC doses in 9-10 week old ob/ob and DIO mice (n = 3-4 per group; Table 1 and
Table 2). The OGTT model was fitted to the glucose-AUC reduction on days 3-6
after single 3 or 10 mg/kg SC doses in ob/ob mice (Fig 3, Fig 6a; at least 8
mice per group and day) and checked against the day-3 dose response to
0.03-10 mg/kg IV or SC (Fig 2, Fig 6b). The body-weight model was fitted to
DIO mice (about 14 weeks on a 60% high-fat diet, about 42-43 g) given 1, 3 or
10 mg/kg IV, or 1 or 10 mg/kg SC, on days 1, 8 and 15 and weighed twice a week
to day 57 (Fig 4, Fig 7; at least 9 mice per group).

```{r population}
str(obob$population)
str(dio$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. They are
collected here.

## ob/ob OGTT model

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lvc` (systemic volume) | 40 mL/kg | Methods, "4% of the body weight" |
| `lka` (SC absorption) | ln(2)/48 1/h | Methods, "absorption half-life of 48 hours" |
| `thalf_ct`, `thalf_nt` (clipping) | 2.5 h, 13 h | Methods, "2.5 and 13 hours for the C and N termini" |
| `thalf_bb` (CovX-2000 backbone) | 12 days | Methods, "~12 days"; Eq 1 |
| `mw` | 192000 g/mol | Not printed; Fig 5a (see Assumptions) |
| `ki` | 0.5 nM | Methods, "KI was set to 0.5 nM" (in vitro pERK EC50) |
| `kn` | 22 nM | Results, "KN was optimized at 22 nM" |
| `gamma` | 3 days | Results, "gamma was optimized at 3 days" |
| `ogtt_a` | 812.74 | Not printed; set so the model equals the day-3 10 mg/kg SC value of Fig 6a |
| 16 species x 2 compartments ODEs | -- | Eq 1 (species [1 1 0 1]) generalised as the text describes; S1 Fig a |
| Intact and N-only pools | -- | Methods, definitions of "intact" and "N-only" |
| `sig` = S(t) | -- | Eq 2 |
| `ogtt_memory`, `ogtt` | -- | Eq 3, written as d/dt(memory) = S - memory/gamma |

## DIO body-weight model

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lka` | ln(2)/48 1/h | Methods, "half-life of 48 hours" |
| `thalf_ct`, `thalf_nt` | 1.7 h, 26.2 h | Methods, "DIO mouse-measured half-lives" |
| `lvc` | 2.4 mL | Methods, "central compartment with volume 2.4 ml" |
| `lvadipose` | 0.8 mL | Methods, "volume 0.8 ml (assuming 20 g of fat with 4% extracellular space)" |
| `lq` | 0.0167 mL/h | Methods, "A first-order transport rate of 0.0167 ml/hr was symmetrically applied" |
| `lkp_adipose` | log(1) | Not printed; implied by "symmetrically applied" (see Assumptions) |
| `mw` | 192000 g/mol | Not printed; Fig 5a |
| `rtot` | 4.15 nM | Methods, receptor complex concentration |
| `kd_intact` | 0.5 nM | Methods, "set to 0.5 nM based on in vitro hASC measurements" |
| `kd_nonly`, `beta`, `delta`, `rho`, `eps` | 94 nM, 1.3, 0.48, 3, 2.3 | Fig 7a table |
| `rmr` | 0.86 kJ/(day g FFM) | Methods, reference 23 |
| `tat_slope`, `tat_int` | 0.46, 9.9 g | Eq 6 |
| `ed_fat`, `ed_lean` | 39.5, 7.6 kJ/g | Methods, reference 22; Eq 7 and Eq 13 |
| `bwc_0`, `bwc_inf`, `kbwc` | 43.25 g, 56.83 g, 0.01226 1/day | Not printed; vehicle curve of Fig 7b, digitised |
| Competitive binding | -- | Eq 4, solved in closed form (cubic in free receptor) |
| `peff` = P(RO) | -- | Eq 5, A = 1 + delta^rho so that P(1) = 1 |
| `fic`, `fi`, `de`, `d/dt(bw)` | -- | Eqs 6-13 (see Assumptions for Eq 8, Eq 11 and Eq 12) |

# ob/ob OGTT model

## PK: intact and N-only pools (Fig 5a) and signalling (Fig 5c)

```{r obob-helpers}
# Before NCA: the ODE solver undershoots zero by about its absolute tolerance
# once a short-lived analyte has gone; assert that, floor it, and drop the
# numerically-zero tail so half-lives are not fitted to integrator noise.
nca_floor <- function(d) {
  d |>
    dplyr::group_by(group, id) |>
    dplyr::filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-6 * max(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()
}
solve_one <- function(mod, ev) {
  out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev))
  if (is.null(out$id)) out$id <- 1L
  out
}
obob_run <- function(dose, route, times = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 168, by = 0.5), 0.083)))) {
  cmt <- if (route == "IV") "central_1111" else "depot_1111"
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, cmt = cmt) |> rxode2::et(times)
  solve_one(obob, ev) |> mutate(route = route, dose = dose)
}
obob_10 <- bind_rows(obob_run(10, "IV"), obob_run(10, "SC"))
```

```{r figure-5a, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5a (and 5c) of Weng 2015: intact (solid) and N-only (dashed) pools after 10 mg/kg IV or SC in ob/ob mice, with the intact (blue) and N-only (green) potencies."}
obob_10 |>
  select(time, route, Intact = Cintact, `N-only` = Cnonly) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Intact, `N-only`), names_to = "pool", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(conc > 0.1) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, conc, colour = route, linetype = pool)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 22, colour = "darkgreen") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1e4)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(IV = "black", SC = "red")) +
  labs(x = "Time after dosing (days)", y = "Calculated plasma concentration (nM)",
       title = "Figure 5a: ob/ob 10 mg/kg")
```

```{r figure-5c, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5c of Weng 2015: instantaneous signal S(t) (shown in the paper as receptor occupancy in the central space)."}
ggplot(obob_10, aes(time / 24, sig, colour = route)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(IV = "black", SC = "red")) +
  labs(x = "Time after dosing (days)", y = "S(t)", title = "Figure 5c: ob/ob 10 mg/kg")
```

Values read from Fig 5a and 5c, against the model:

```{r fig5a-check}
at <- function(d, route, t) d[d$route == route & abs(d$time - t) < 1e-6, ]
fig5a <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~figure, ~model,
  "IV intact at t = 0 (nM)", 1300, at(obob_10, "IV", 0)$Cintact,
  "SC N-only peak (nM)", 180, max(obob_10$Cnonly[obob_10$route == "SC"]),
  "IV and SC N-only at day 7 (nM)", 0.23, at(obob_10, "IV", 168)$Cnonly,
  "IV S(t) at day 2", 0.88, at(obob_10, "IV", 48)$sig,
  "IV S(t) at day 3", 0.70, at(obob_10, "IV", 72)$sig
)
knitr::kable(fig5a, digits = 2)
stopifnot(abs(fig5a$model / fig5a$figure - 1) < 0.1)
```

The figure values are approximate readings of a log-scale plot; the model
values agree within 10%. The 1300 nM starting value is what fixed the
unprinted molecular weight (see Assumptions), so that row is not an
independent check.

## Mass balance of the clipping network

Every clipping reaction turns one species into another, so the total amount
of molecules in the depot and central compartments falls only through
backbone clearance in the central compartment. The check uses the same
solve (no closed form is involved beyond integration).

```{r obob-mass-balance}
states <- grep("^(depot|central)_[01]{4}$", names(obob_10), value = TRUE)
mb <- obob_10 |>
  filter(route == "IV") |>
  mutate(total = rowSums(across(all_of(states))))
# IV dose: only central species exist and all are lost at kbb = ln(2)/288 1/h
mb_err <- max(abs(mb$total - 10 * exp(-log(2) / 288 * mb$time)))
mb_err
stopifnot(mb_err < 1e-4)
```

## PKNCA: the two ELISA analytes against Table 1 and Table 2

The two assays detect every molecule with at least one intact C-terminus
(CT assay, `Cct`) or one intact N-terminus (NT assay, `Cnt`). The model
outputs are in nM; they are converted to ug/mL with the molecular weight.

```{r obob-pknca}
obob_nca_in <- obob_10 |>
  select(id, time, route, CT = Cct, NT = Cnt) |>
  pivot_longer(c(CT, NT), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc_nM") |>
  mutate(Cc = conc_nM * 192000 / 1e6, group = paste("ob/ob", analyte, route)) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)
stopifnot(all(obob_nca_in$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(obob_nca_in$Cc)))
obob_nca_in <- nca_floor(obob_nca_in)
# dose in ug/kg with concentrations in ug/mL gives CL in mL/h/kg
obob_dose <- obob_nca_in |> distinct(id, group) |> mutate(time = 0, dose = 10000)
obob_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(obob_nca_in, Cc ~ time | group + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(obob_dose, dose ~ time | group + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE)
))
obob_res <- as.data.frame(obob_nca)
```

## OGTT time course (Fig 6a) and dose response (Fig 6b)

`ogtt_a` was set by the authors so that the model matches the observed
day-3 response to 10 mg/kg SC. Fig 6b uses a second normalisation, matched to
the 10 mg/kg IV point ("In this case the model output normalization was set
to the 10 mg/kg IV dose"); it is applied here by overriding `ogtt_a`.

```{r figure-6a}
ogtt_days <- c(3, 4, 5, 6)
fig6a <- bind_rows(lapply(c(3, 10), function(d) {
  obob_run(d, "SC", times = ogtt_days * 24) |>
    transmute(dose = d, day = time / 24, model = ogtt)
})) |>
  mutate(
    # Fig 6a, digitised: model crosses and observed means ((mg/dL)*min)
    figure_model = c(21900, 19100, 14800, 11200, 29800, 28850, 23850, 18000),
    data = c(22200, 16800, 16700, 10300, 29900, 28850, 25200, 19800)
  )
knitr::kable(fig6a, digits = 0)
stopifnot(abs(fig6a$model / fig6a$figure_model - 1) < 0.05)
```

```{r figure-6a-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6a of Weng 2015: OGTT glucose-AUC reduction 3-6 days after a single SC dose. Circles: observed means read from the figure; crosses: model."}
ggplot(fig6a, aes(day, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_point(aes(y = data), shape = 1, size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(y = model), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("3" = "red", "10" = "blue"), name = "mg/kg SC") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = "Time after dosing (days)", y = "delta(AUC) (mg/dL)*min", title = "Figure 6a")
```

```{r figure-6b}
iv10_memory <- obob_run(10, "IV", times = 72)$ogtt_memory
obob_6b <- obob |> rxode2::ini(ogtt_a = 23500 / iv10_memory)
fig6b <- expand.grid(dose = c(0.03, 0.3, 1, 3, 10), route = c("IV", "SC"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fig6b$model <- mapply(function(d, r) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = d, cmt = if (r == "IV") "central_1111" else "depot_1111") |> rxode2::et(72)
  solve_one(obob_6b, ev)$ogtt
}, fig6b$dose, fig6b$route)
# Fig 6b, digitised: model crosses and observed means ((mg/dL)*min)
fig6b$figure_model <- c(3000, 9000, 14300, 19000, 23500, 600, 4400, 9500, 15700, 21500)
fig6b$data <- c(6000, 12900, 16300, 18700, 23500, 5900, 7900, 12700, 12700, 16300)
knitr::kable(fig6b, digits = 0)
# The 0.03 mg/kg crosses sit at the bottom of the axis, where one pixel is
# ~80 units; compare the remaining doses on a relative scale.
big <- fig6b$dose >= 0.3
stopifnot(abs(fig6b$model[big] / fig6b$figure_model[big] - 1) < 0.07)
```

```{r figure-6b-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 6b of Weng 2015: day-3 OGTT dose response. Circles: observed means read from the figure; crosses: model."}
ggplot(fig6b, aes(factor(dose), colour = route)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = data), shape = 1, size = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(y = model), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(IV = "red", SC = "blue")) +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg/kg)", y = "delta(AUC) (mg/dL)*min", title = "Figure 6b")
```

The packaged ob/ob model reproduces both panels of Fig 6 to within a few
percent of the plotted model crosses, and the pools and signal of Fig 5a/5c.

# DIO body-weight model

## Central-adipose exchange: printed value and the reading that matches the figures

The Methods give the exchange between the central compartment (2.4 mL) and
the adipose extracellular space (0.8 mL) as "a first-order transport rate of
0.0167 ml/hr ... symmetrically applied", which "corresponds to the fat
extracellular volume exchanging with the plasma over 48 hours" (0.8 mL / 48 h
= 0.0167 mL/h). The packaged model uses exactly that: a flow `q` of
0.0167 mL/h acting on the concentration difference, which makes the
steady-state volume Vc + Vadipose = 3.2 mL, the "7% total Vss" of a 45 g mouse
the paper quotes.

Read that way, the model does not reproduce the authors' own simulated
figures: adipose exposure (Fig 5b), adipose receptor occupancy (Fig 5d) and
the body-weight loss of Fig 7b/7c are all well below what the paper shows.
Fig 5b has the adipose N-only concentration (~850 nM after 10 mg/kg IV)
*above* the highest central N-only concentration the same PK produces (about
730 nM), which no flow-limited exchange with an equal concentration ratio can
do. An exchange with the same first-order rate constant on the *amounts* in
both directions can, and with a rate constant of about 0.05 1/h (read from
the shape of Fig 5b, not fitted to body weight) it reproduces Fig 5b and 5d
and comes close to Fig 7b and 7c. In this model's
parameters that reading is `q = 0.05 * 2.4 = 0.12` mL/h with an
adipose:central concentration ratio `kp_adipose = Vc / Vadipose = 3`. It is
shown below as an `ini()` override, next to the packaged (printed) model.

```{r dio-models}
dio_alt <- dio |> rxode2::ini(lq = log(0.05 * 2.4), lkp_adipose = log(2.4 / 0.8))
dio_models <- list(printed = dio, `figure-matching` = dio_alt)

# Vehicle curves: IV study (Fig 7b; the model default) and SC study (Fig 7c),
# both digitised and fitted to bwc_inf - (bwc_inf - bwc_0) * exp(-kbwc * day).
sc_vehicle <- c(bwc_0 = 41.667, bwc_inf = 68.585, kbwc = 0.006027)

# Doses are per 45 g mouse, the body weight the PK volumes are built for.
dio_run <- function(mod, dose, route, wt_base, times = seq(0, 56 * 24, by = 2), n_doses = 3) {
  if (route == "SC") mod <- mod |> rxode2::ini(bwc_0 = sc_vehicle[["bwc_0"]],
                                             bwc_inf = sc_vehicle[["bwc_inf"]],
                                             kbwc = sc_vehicle[["kbwc"]])
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose * 0.045, cmt = if (route == "IV") "central" else "depot",
                   ii = 168, addl = n_doses - 1) |>
    rxode2::et(times) |>
    as.data.frame()
  ev$WT_BASE <- wt_base
  solve_one(mod, ev) |> mutate(dose = dose, route = route)
}
# Group starting weights read from Fig 7b/7c (kg)
arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~route, ~wt_base,
  1, "IV", 0.04325, 3, "IV", 0.04325, 10, "IV", 0.04325,
  1, "SC", 0.04236, 10, "SC", 0.04207
)
dio_sims <- bind_rows(lapply(names(dio_models), function(nm) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
    dio_run(dio_models[[nm]], arms$dose[i], arms$route[i], arms$wt_base[i])
  })) |> mutate(reading = nm)
}))
```

## PK and receptor occupancy in adipose (Fig 5b, 5d)

```{r figure-5b, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5b of Weng 2015: intact (solid) and N-only (dashed) concentrations in adipose after 10 mg/kg weekly x3, packaged (printed exchange) and figure-matching readings."}
dio_sims |>
  filter(dose == 10, time <= 35 * 24) |>
  select(time, route, reading, Intact = Cadipose, `N-only` = Cadipose_nonly) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Intact, `N-only`), names_to = "pool", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(conc > 0.1) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, conc, colour = route, linetype = pool)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 94, colour = "darkgreen") +
  facet_wrap(~reading) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(IV = "black", SC = "red")) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Calculated concentration in adipose (nM)", title = "Figure 5b: DIO 10 mg/kg")
```

```{r figure-5d, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5d of Weng 2015: receptor occupancy in adipose after 10 mg/kg weekly x3."}
dio_sims |>
  filter(dose == 10, time <= 35 * 24) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, ro, colour = route)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~reading) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(IV = "black", SC = "red")) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Receptor occupancy", title = "Figure 5d: DIO 10 mg/kg")
```

```{r fig5bd-check}
first_week <- dio_sims |> filter(dose == 10, time < 168)
fig5bd <- first_week |>
  group_by(reading, route) |>
  summarise(
    `adipose N-only peak (nM)` = max(Cadipose_nonly),
    `adipose intact peak (nM)` = max(Cadipose),
    `RO at day 1` = ro[time == 24],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
fig5bd_ref <- tibble::tibble(
  reading = "Fig 5b/5d (read from figure)", route = c("IV", "SC"),
  `adipose N-only peak (nM)` = c(850, 160), `adipose intact peak (nM)` = c(100, 2),
  `RO at day 1` = c(0.95, 0.6)
)
knitr::kable(bind_rows(fig5bd, fig5bd_ref), digits = 2)
```

## Transfer function P(RO) (Fig 7d)

```{r figure-7d, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 7d of Weng 2015."}
p_ro <- function(ro, delta = 0.48, rho = 3) (delta^rho + 1) * ro^rho / (delta^rho + ro^rho)
ro_grid <- seq(0, 1, by = 0.01)
ggplot(data.frame(ro = ro_grid, p = p_ro(ro_grid)), aes(ro, p)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Receptor occupancy", y = "Relative effect on BW", title = "Figure 7d")
stopifnot(abs(p_ro(1) - 1) < 1e-12, abs(p_ro(0.48) - 0.5 * (0.48^3 + 1)) < 1e-12)
```

## Receptor binding: closed-form solution against the equations it solves

The model solves Eq 4 in closed form. Plugging its free-receptor value back
into the receptor mass balance checks the root (and its branch) at every
output time of every arm.

```{r binding-check}
kdi <- 0.5; kdn <- 94; rt <- 4.15
bind_chk <- dio_sims |>
  mutate(
    resid = rfree + Cadipose * rfree / (kdi + rfree) +
      Cadipose_nonly * rfree / (kdn + rfree) - rt
  )
max(abs(bind_chk$resid))
stopifnot(max(abs(bind_chk$resid)) < 1e-8, all(bind_chk$rfree > 0 & bind_chk$rfree <= rt + 1e-12))
```

## Body weight (Fig 7b, 7c)

```{r figure-7bc, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 7b (IV) and 7c (SC) of Weng 2015: body weight after three weekly doses, packaged (printed exchange) and figure-matching readings. The black curve is the vehicle-group input curve of each study."}
vehicle <- bind_rows(
  dio_sims |> filter(dose == 1, route == "IV") |> distinct(time, reading, route, bw = bwc),
  dio_sims |> filter(dose == 1, route == "SC") |> distinct(time, reading, route, bw = bwc)
) |> mutate(arm = "Vehicle")
dio_sims |>
  mutate(arm = paste(dose, "mg/kg")) |>
  select(time, reading, route, arm, bw) |>
  bind_rows(vehicle) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, bw, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(reading ~ route) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Vehicle = "black", `1 mg/kg` = "red", `3 mg/kg` = "green3", `10 mg/kg` = "blue")) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "BW (g)", title = "Figures 7b and 7c")
```

Nadirs of the model curves, against the model curves of Fig 7b/7c:

```{r fig7-check}
fig7 <- dio_sims |>
  group_by(reading, route, dose) |>
  summarise(nadir_g = min(bw), nadir_day = time[which.min(bw)] / 24, day56_g = bw[time == 56 * 24], .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~route, ~dose, ~figure_nadir_g, ~figure_nadir_day,
      "IV", 1, 41.9, 3, "IV", 3, 40.5, 17, "IV", 10, 37.5, 18,
      "SC", 1, NA, NA, "SC", 10, 39.5, 18
    ),
    by = c("route", "dose")
  ) |>
  arrange(route, dose, reading)
knitr::kable(fig7, digits = 2)
# Deterministic solves, so these bounds only need to cover the reading error
# of the figure (~0.1 g) and the reported misses.
alt_fig7 <- fig7 |> filter(reading == "figure-matching", !is.na(figure_nadir_g), dose >= 3)
printed_fig7 <- fig7 |> filter(reading == "printed", dose == 10)
stopifnot(
  abs(alt_fig7$nadir_g - alt_fig7$figure_nadir_g) < 1.2,
  # the printed exchange loses at least 1.5 g less than Fig 7b/7c at 10 mg/kg
  printed_fig7$nadir_g - printed_fig7$figure_nadir_g > 1.5
)
```

With the printed exchange, the packaged model gives a 10 mg/kg IV nadir of
about 40 g against 37.5 g in Fig 7b, and almost no loss after 10 mg/kg SC
(Fig 7c: about 39.5 g). The figure-matching reading reproduces the 3 and
10 mg/kg IV nadirs to within about 0.4 g and their timing, and puts the
10 mg/kg SC nadir about 1 g below Fig 7c (38.5 against 39.5 g; the SC
study's own vehicle curve and starting weight are used). Neither reading
reproduces the early dip of the 1 mg/kg IV curve (about 41.9 g at day 3 in
Fig 7b).

## Vehicle self-consistency

With no drug, P = 0 and a treated animal that starts on the vehicle curve
must stay on it (Eq 8 defines vehicle food intake from that curve).

```{r vehicle-check}
veh_ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 56 * 24, by = 24), evid = 0, amt = 0,
                     cmt = "central", WT_BASE = 0.04325)
veh <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(dio, veh_ev))
max(abs(veh$bw - veh$bwc))
stopifnot(max(abs(veh$bw - veh$bwc)) < 1e-3)
```

## PKNCA: DIO PK against Table 1 and Table 2

In the DIO model the intact molecule is what the CT assay detects, and the
intact plus N-only molecules are what the NT assay detects. Single 10 mg/kg
doses (per 45 g) with the packaged model:

```{r dio-pknca}
pk_times <- c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), seq(25, 480, by = 1))
dio_pk <- bind_rows(
  dio_run(dio, 10, "IV", 0.04325, times = pk_times, n_doses = 1),
  dio_run(dio, 10, "SC", 0.04325, times = pk_times, n_doses = 1)
)
dio_nca_in <- dio_pk |>
  transmute(id, time, route, CT = Cc, NT = Cc + Cc_nonly) |>
  pivot_longer(c(CT, NT), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc_nM") |>
  mutate(Cc = conc_nM * 192000 / 1e6, group = paste("DIO", analyte, route)) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)
stopifnot(all(dio_nca_in$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(dio_nca_in$Cc)))
dio_nca_in <- nca_floor(dio_nca_in)
dio_dose <- dio_nca_in |> distinct(id, group) |> mutate(time = 0, dose = 10000)
dio_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(dio_nca_in, Cc ~ time | group + id),
  # dose in ug/kg with concentrations in ug/mL gives CL in mL/h/kg
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dio_dose, dose ~ time | group + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, cl.obs = TRUE)
))
dio_res <- as.data.frame(dio_nca)
```

```{r nca-comparison}
sim_long <- bind_rows(obob_res, dio_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("half.life", "cl.obs", "tmax")) |>
  filter(!(grepl("SC", group) & PPTESTCD == "cl.obs")) |>
  select(group, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
# Table 1 (IV) and Table 2 (SC), means. CL is not reported for SC; the NT
# half-life of ob/ob SC and its Cmax are not used (NC / dose not stated).
ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~half.life, ~cl.obs, ~tmax,
  "ob/ob CT IV", 2.20, 20.2, NA,
  "ob/ob NT IV", 13.0, 3.25, NA,
  "ob/ob CT SC", 2.48, NA, 6.0,
  "ob/ob NT SC", NA, NA, 21.0,
  "DIO CT IV", 1.61, 18.8, NA,
  "DIO NT IV", 22.7, 2.62, NA,
  "DIO CT SC", 3.61, NA, 4.0,
  "DIO NT SC", 55.1, NA, 19.0
)
sim_long <- sim_long |> semi_join(
  ref |> pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "PPTESTCD") |> filter(!is.na(value)),
  by = c("group", "PPTESTCD")
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_long, ref, by = "group",
  units = c(half.life = "h", cl.obs = "mL/h/kg", tmax = "h")
)
# Only IV clearances are compared, so the row is CL, not CL/F
cmp[[1]] <- sub("CL/F", "CL", cmp[[1]], fixed = TRUE)
knitr::kable(cmp)
```

`r attr(cmp, "footnote")`

The models use the clipping half-lives the authors chose (ob/ob 2.5 and
13 h; DIO 1.7 and 26.2 h), which are close to but not equal to the Table 1
means, so the IV half-lives agree within about 15%. Clearances agree less
well: the models were built to reproduce the clipping kinetics and the PD,
not the volume terms of the NCA (ob/ob uses a volume of 40 mL/kg against a
Table 1 Vc of 22.5-24.2 mL/kg; the ob/ob CT analyte also includes the
long-lived molecules whose N-terminus was clipped first). After SC dosing the
model's terminal half-lives equal its clipping half-lives, because loss from
the depot (absorption plus clipping) is faster than clipping alone; the
longer SC half-lives of Table 2 (3.6 h and 55 h in DIO) are not reproduced,
and neither are the Tmax values of the DIO arm. These rows are shown as they
are and were not tuned.

The DIO Methods also state that this PK model "leads to calculated
bioavailabilities of 2.6% and 38.5% for intact CT and NT respectively
following subcutaneous dosing, a Tmax ~24 hours for the intact NT":

```{r dio-f}
auc <- dio_res |> filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |> select(group, PPORRES)
f_ct <- auc$PPORRES[auc$group == "DIO CT SC"] / auc$PPORRES[auc$group == "DIO CT IV"]
f_nt <- auc$PPORRES[auc$group == "DIO NT SC"] / auc$PPORRES[auc$group == "DIO NT IV"]
# Closed form: fraction of the depot dose absorbed before clipping
ka <- log(2) / 48; kct <- log(2) / 1.7; knt <- log(2) / 26.2
c(F_CT = f_ct, F_CT_closed_form = ka / (ka + kct + knt),
  F_NT = f_nt, F_NT_closed_form = ka / (ka + knt))
stopifnot(abs(f_ct / (ka / (ka + kct + knt)) - 1) < 0.01, abs(f_nt / (ka / (ka + knt)) - 1) < 0.01)
tmax_nt <- dio_res |> filter(group == "DIO NT SC", PPTESTCD == "tmax") |> pull(PPORRES)
tmax_nt
```

The model gives 3.2% and 35.3%, against the 2.6% and 38.5% the paper quotes
for the same model, and an NT Tmax of about `r round(tmax_nt)` hours (paper:
~24 hours). The printed bioavailabilities cannot both come from one
absorption half-life (2.6% implies 60 h, 38.5% implies 42 h), so they may
have been computed over a finite window or with settings not given in the
paper.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Central-adipose exchange (DIO).** Packaged as printed: a flow of
  0.0167 mL/h between equal concentrations (`kp_adipose = 1`). This
  under-predicts the paper's own Fig 5b, 5d, 7b and 7c (see above). An
  exchange with a rate constant of about 0.05 1/h on amounts in both
  directions (`q = 0.12` mL/h, `kp_adipose = 3` in this parameterisation)
  reproduces Fig 5b and 5d and comes within about 1 g of the Fig 7b/7c
  nadirs. The 0.05 1/h was read from Fig 5b; the paper
  prints neither it nor `kp_adipose`, which exists in the model only so the
  alternative can be expressed as an `ini()` override.
* **Molecular weight.** Not printed. 192 kDa makes a 10 mg/kg IV dose in
  4% of body weight start at the ~1300 nM of Fig 5a; with it the ob/ob
  model reproduces Fig 6a and 6b. It is consistent with an IgG scaffold
  carrying two FGF21 molecules (roughly 150 + 2 x 19.5 kDa).
* **OGTT normalisation A.** Not printed. Set so the model equals the
  day-3 response to 10 mg/kg SC in Fig 6a (29900 (mg/dL)*min, read from the
  figure) for Fig 6a, and to the 10 mg/kg IV point (23500) for Fig 6b, as
  the Results describe.
* **Vehicle body-weight curve (DIO).** The paper smooths the vehicle data to
  estimate vehicle food intake but gives no smoothing function. The vehicle
  model curves of Fig 7b (IV study, packaged default) and Fig 7c (SC study,
  set by override above) were digitised and fitted with an exponential
  approach (residual SD about 0.1 g). Group starting weights were read from
  the same figures.
* **Eq 8 energy densities.** Eq 8 writes the energy content of added tissue
  as 0.46 x 7.6 + 0.54 x 39.5 kJ/g, transposing the fat and lean
  coefficients of Eq 7 and Eq 13 (0.46 x 39.5 + 0.54 x 7.6, from 46% body
  fat). The model uses the Eq 7/Eq 13 value throughout; with the printed
  Eq 8 a vehicle animal would grow 11% faster than the vehicle curve it is
  built from.
* **Sign of the FGF21 energy term.** Eq 11 defines dE_FGF21 = -epsilon P TAT
  and Eq 12 subtracts it, which as printed would add energy and increase
  body weight. The text describes it as "an additional energy consumption
  term" (browning, thermogenesis), so the model subtracts epsilon P TAT from
  the energy balance.
* **Units of epsilon.** Fig 7a gives epsilon in kJ/(day g FFM), but Eq 11 and
  the text ("proportional to the amount of body fat") apply it to total
  adipose tissue. The model follows Eq 11; applying it to fat-free mass
  instead gives a 10 mg/kg IV nadir near 29 g with the packaged exchange,
  far below Fig 7b (37.5 g).
* **Baseline food intake.** FI(t = 0) in Eq 10 is taken as Eq 10 evaluated at
  t = 0, where P = 0: vehicle intake at day 0 scaled by
  (BWcontrol(0) / BW(0))^beta. For groups starting on the vehicle curve this
  is the vehicle intake.
* **RMR units.** The Methods give 0.86 kJ/(g fat free mass); per day is
  implied by the food-intake units and the reference.
* **Dose basis (DIO).** Doses are converted to mg for a 45 g mouse, the body
  weight the PK volumes are built for. Body weight in the PD part does not
  feed back into the PK.
* **Receptor binding.** Eq 4 is solved exactly (the free receptor is the
  root of a cubic), not by numerical iteration; the check above confirms the
  root at every output time.
* **No variability.** The paper estimates no between-animal or residual
  variability; neither model has etas or residual error.
